newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Granada H1 growth to quiet doubters.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Granada H1 growth to quiet doubters.

text.p: Granada Group Plc is expected to deliver first half profit growth of some 30 percent which should quell murmurs of discontent about delay in its hotel disposals, analysts said.

Analysts are forecasting pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit in the 235-240 million stg range in the six months to end-March, against 183.3 million stg a year ago. The media and leisure company, which reports on Wednesday, is expected to pay an interim dividend of 4.7-4.8 pence per share, up from 4.235p.
"The market is preoccupied with hotel disposal progress and that has been slow but the stock is undervalued on fundamentals," said Greg Feehely of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
Feehely, who continues to rate the stock a "buy", noted Granada had underperformed the market by nine percent over the last 12 months and its sector by 1.5 percent.
Confidence in the Granada management team was one of the key factors in the company's success in its 3.9 billion stg hostile bid for hotel and catering empire Forte in 1995/96.
But analysts say there is a hint of impatience over the uneven progress on hotel disposals.
Granada put 17 Exclusive 'luxury' hotels up for sale last year but has only sold seven of them and taken the largest, London's Grosvenor House, off the market.
Granada points out that the hotel disposals have raised more than 400 million stg, at a premium to book value of 65 million stg.
The company has raised over 1.2 billion stg from disposals since it acquired Forte in January 1996.
It achieved a premium to book value of 142 million stg on the sale of its Welcome Break motorway service areas to Bahrain-based Invest Corp for 476 million earlier this year.

That gain will be one of a number of exceptional items in the company's first half reports. It is expected to post one-off gains of some 40 million on hotel sales in the period plus eight million stg on the sale of its stake in Alpha Airports.

These gains will largely be balanced by a 160 million stg write-off against the value of its computer services arm. The value is being written down to 40 million stg and the unit is expected to be sold shortly.
It will take a 10 million stg charge to cover the cost of closing some 100 UK high street rental stores.

Granada's media arm is part of a consortium with BSkyB and Carlton Communications bidding for licences to operate new digital terrestrial television services. The ITC is expected to announce who has won the licences in the next few weeks.
Granada owns ITV franchises for London Weekend Television and north-west England. It has a 27 percent stake in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television but has ruled out a bid for the time being.
